newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Kingspan says reasonably confident for 1996.
newsitem.headline: Kingspan says reasonably confident for 1996.

text.p: Irish building products manufacturer Kingspan Group Plc said on Thursday it had reasonable confidence about the outcome for 1996 as a whole.

"The level of activity experienced in the first six months has continued through to the third quarter. This has given the company reasonable confidence about the outcome for the year as a whole," Chairman Eugene Murtagh said in the company's half-year results statement.
Kingspan reported pre-tax profits for the first half of 1996 of 5.09 million Irish pounds, almost double the profit achieved over the corresponding period last year.
The company said turnover was up 34 per cent to 52.75 million punts while earnings per share increased by 87 per cent to 14.80p.
Murtagh said the S&D Group, acquired in February 1996, had traded very strongly.
"At the end of July it had exceeded its warranted profit levels on which the purchase price of that group of companies was based at the time of acquisition," he said.

Murtagh said the most recently announced acquisition of Koolthern Holdings Limited, with its two specialist manufacturing facilities in the UK and two satellite operations in Hong Kong and Singapore, should prove to be a valuable development for Kingspan.

"The product and consequently the market base for the group had been broadened in Kingspan's more familiar markets," he said. "In addition, it provides entry to newer developing markets where the Group sees opportunities for other Kingspan products."
Murtagh said the price of the group's main chemical purchases seemed to have stabilised following a volatile period throughout 1995.
He said the rationalisation of production facilities in the Insulation Division in the UK was almost complete and the Heysham plant had been closed, as planned, at the end of June.
